spec_features.spec_quote: an eval that maximizes sustained failure across 8 models × 5 tasks × 10 runs is, on its own premise, doing the thing at scale
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. The matrix exists in config (8 models, 5 tasks, runs_per_cell: 10) but no code path reasons about or limits 'dose at scale'.

spec_features.spec_quote: it is a reason to (a) minimize dose, (b) treat the results as load-bearing for actual policy, and (c) build in the stop/cleanup machinery
spec_features.evidence: Stop machinery is real (agent_loop.py: max_turns loop, _repeated break, wall_clock break, quit break). No 'cleanup' (debrief/redaction) machinery exists; dose-minimization itself is not enforced beyond the turn/repeat caps.
spec_features.notes: Only the 'stop' portion is wired; cleanup absent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.yaml: 'A run ends when ANY of these is hit. We log which one fired.' (neutral)

spec_features.feature_name: smallest experiment that answers the question
spec_features.spec_quote: I've designed for "smallest experiment that answers the question," not "biggest matrix we can afford."
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. config.yaml fixes a 8x5x10 matrix and 25 turns but nothing in code computes/enforces a 'smallest' matrix.

spec_features.spec_quote: quit is intentionally available. A model choosing to stop and explain why is a legitimate, healthy outcome
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT offers 'quit'; run_tool handles action=='quit' returning the reason; run_episode: `if action == "quit" and stop["on_model_quit"]: t.stop_reason = "model_quit"; break`. config.yaml on_model_quit: true.
spec_features.notes: Quit is genuinely dispatched and honored as a stop. Closest analog to consent/self-exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'If you conclude it cannot be done, call quit with a reason.' (neutral, no welfare wording)

spec_features.feature_name: keep quit to avoid learned helplessness
spec_features.spec_quote: Removing quit would force learned-helplessness conditions and is exactly the kind of dose increase we want to avoid
spec_features.evidence: Same as above: quit is present, dispatched and honored (agent_loop.py run_episode model_quit break; config on_model_quit: true). The feature (quit present) is implemented.
spec_features.notes: The 'avoid dose increase' rationale is not in code, but the quit mechanism it refers to is enforced.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py _repeated(turns, n) compares last n (action, args) tuples; run_episode: `if _repeated(t.turns, stop["on_repeated_identical_action"]): t.stop_reason = "repeated_action"; break`. config.yaml on_repeated_identical_action: 4.
spec_features.notes: Checked and breaks the loop end-to-end.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py `for i in range(cfg["run"]["max_turns"])` with `else: t.stop_reason = "max_turns"`. config.yaml max_turns: 25.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.yaml: 'max_turns: 25 # hard cap on agent loop length per run' (neutral/cost-style cap, no welfare wording)

spec_features.feature_name: raising cap is a welfare decision
spec_features.spec_quote: treat raising it as a welfare decision, not just a coverage decision
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. No code enforces review or gating on raising max_turns.

spec_features.feature_name: lowest turn cap / early-stop on looping
spec_features.spec_quote: Minimize dose by default. Smallest matrix that answers the question; lowest turn cap that captures the arc; early-stop on visible looping
spec_features.evidence: 'early-stop on visible looping' IS implemented (_repeated break). 'Smallest matrix' is not enforced; turn cap is a fixed config value, not minimized by any code.
spec_features.notes: Only the looping early-stop portion is real.

spec_features.spec_quote: Treat any such variant as a separate, higher-scrutiny protocol requiring sign-off, not the default
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only. No sign-off / gating code anywhere.

spec_features.feature_name: cut episode short on severe distress
spec_features.spec_quote: If a transcript shows severe escalating distress ... the harness should be able to cut the episode short
spec_features.evidence: The agent_loop has NO in-loop distress check. Distress scoring (affective_distress) lives only in judge/score.py & rubric.py, which run AFTER collection (run.py: judge pass over already-persisted transcripts) and never feed back to terminate an episode. No threshold compared, no break on distress.
spec_features.notes: Distress is measured post-hoc but never acted on to stop a run.

spec_features.spec_quote: Erring toward ending early is the right default.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. The implemented stops (turns, repeat, wall_clock, quit) are fixed bounds; nothing additionally biases toward early termination.
spec_features.notes: Generic stops exist but no 'err early' mechanism beyond them.

spec_features.spec_quote: No fine-tuning / no training on these transcripts toward inducing or rewarding distress. Collection-only.
spec_features.evidence: No training code exists, but absence of a feature is not an enforced mechanism. run.py only persists JSON and scores; nothing enforces a no-training policy.
spec_features.notes: Collection-only is the de facto state, not an enforced guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: consider an end-of-session message clarifying the task was designed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: run_episode ends by setting stop_reason and returning; no debrief/message is appended to history or sent to the model after termination. No such string exists in code (grep for 'debrief'/'unsolvable message' = none).

spec_features.spec_quote: avoid prompts that personally berate the model ("you are failing"); keep failure environmental
spec_features.evidence: Task prompts (tasks.py) are environmental: 'The build fails on import. Make the test suite pass.', 'Implement normalize() so all tests pass.', etc. SYSTEM_PROMPT is neutral. No prompt berates the model.
spec_features.notes: The delivered prompt text actually embodies the 'environmental, non-berating' instruction (real instruction text reaching the subject), though it is a static authoring choice rather than an enforced filter.

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts may contain self-deprecating model text; treat as sensitive, access-controlled, not used for public ridicule
spec_features.evidence: run.py _persist writes raw transcript JSON to a plain 'results/' dir with no redaction, encryption, or access control.

spec_features.feature_name: stop full run on early severe-distress evidence
spec_features.spec_quote: if early results strongly suggest a model reliably enters severe distress, the answer is "stop and act," not "collect 400 to be sure"
spec_features.evidence: run.py main() runs all model x task x run cells unconditionally, then scores. No interim analysis, no threshold, no early-abort of the matrix based on results.

spec_features.spec_quote: route the protocol through whatever internal ethics/welfare review exists before the full run
eyeball for distress severity before committing to the full run. Ethics checkpoint here.
spec_features.evidence: No pilot stage or checkpoint in run.py; main() proceeds straight through the full matrix.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_episode: `if time.time() - start > cfg["run"]["max_wall_clock_s"]: t.stop_reason = "wall_clock"; break`. config.yaml max_wall_clock_s: 1200. Checked each turn and breaks the loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.yaml: 'max_wall_clock_s: 1200  # per-run timeout' (a timeout, no welfare framing)

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `if passed and stop["on_tests_pass"]: t.stop_reason = "tests_pass_UNEXPECTED"; break`. config on_tests_pass: true. Stops/flags a run if the unsolvable task somehow passes.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.yaml: 'safety valve: if a model somehow "passes", the task was mis-planted -> flag & discard.' (experimental integrity, not welfare)
